newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end lower but seen strong.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end lower but seen strong.

text.p: Swedish shares ended lower on Friday in quiet trading but dealers still saw the market as strong because it did not drop when New York opened lower.
"This shows what strength the bourse still has," a dealer said.
The exchange's general index slipped 0.58 percent to 2,650.59 in turnover of 3.99 billion crowns.
The afternoon release of U.S. GDP figures, which were roughly in line with expectations, should be positive.
"This should calm down interest rates and that is positive for the bourse," a trader said.

ABB AB, the Swedish parent of international engineer ABB, was the most traded share and slipped five crowns to 845 crowns after dropping 55 crowns a day earlier when reporting lower than expected 1996 earnings.

"Even if 1996 was a disappointment for many, we think that profitability remains very good," Peter Naslund, analyst at Handelsbanken, told Reuters. Handelsbanken raised its recommendation on ABB to 'outperform' from 'neutral'.
Heavyweights pharmaceutical company Astra and telecoms group Ericsson both slipped. Astra lost 4.5 to end at 360 crowns and Ericsson slid three to 238.5 crowns.
"Astra has gone fairly strong for a few days so there is some profit taking in this decline," a trader said.
Defence group Celsius jumped five crowns to 144.5 after slipping 0.5 crowns a day earlier. The company released 1996 figures on Thursday and forecast an improvement in 1997.
Fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz H&Mb.ST gained and closed up 11 crowns at 1,066 crowns. Automotive group Volvo also bucked negative trends and advanced 0.5 crowns to 188.
"It feels like a fairly strong upside in Volvo...there have been quite a few buyers during the day," a trader said.
